headlines.article_text: Widespread Microsoft outage takes down Outlook and other 365 services Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points A Microsoft outage on Thursday affected users of services like Outlook, Teams and 365. Amazon Web Services said it was "operating normally" and noted inaccurate reports of outages on its platforms. Google users reported issues on DownDetector. In this article MSFT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A sign on the Microsoft campus in Redmond, Washington, US, Oct. 26, 2026. David Ryder | Reuters Microsoft suffered a widespread outage on Thursday that impacted thousands of users across regions, according to outage-tracking website Downdetector.com . The outage began shortly before 1 p.m. and impacted Microsoft 365 services, Outlook and Teams. Amazon Web Services and Google users also reported outages on the site. "We are aware and investigating reports of users experiencing issues with Microsoft 365 services, primarily issues with Exchange Online," a Microsoft spokesperson wrote in a statement to CNBC. "We appreciate our customers' patience while we work to restore services as soon as possible." Microsoft shared updates from its Microsoft 365 Status account on social media platform X. Amazon said its services were "operating normally" and an "unrelated disruption elsewhere on the internet is prompting some inaccurate news reports" in a post to X. The company referred users to its health dashboard for "accurate data." At 4 p.m. , Microsoft said it had "validated an alternative service health check method" that brought some affected servers back online. "We're now applying this change more broadly," Microsoft wrote. "We're also preparing automated recovery systems to continually detect and restart unresponsive servers, to maintain service stability while this change progresses." Microsoft initially wrote that some infrastructure "elevated load across multiple regions" was responsible for the connectivity problems. The company later determined that the elevated load was caused by a "number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable; straining the remaining infrastructure" and that some servers were failing automated health checks. "We've taken steps to prevent additional servers from being impacted while we work to return the affected servers to service," Microsoft wrote . David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Cerebras Systems reported better-than-expected revenue and quarterly guidance in its earnings report on Thursday, and touted a new deal with Microsoft . The stock soared 18% in extended trading. Here's how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus: Loss per share: 67 cents. It's not immediately clear how the number compares with the loss of 14 cents expected Core revenue: $230.9 million vs. $214.7 million expected Cerebras' core revenue grew 70% from $135.7 million, compared with 103% growth in the second quarter, according to a statement . "I think there is opportunity created by, particularly on the hardware side, the sale of hardware, where long lead times in GPUs and more expense creates opportunity for us," Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman told CNBC in an interview, referring to graphics processing units. Executives will announce a new relationship with Microsoft , one of the world's top cloud providers, on a conference call with analysts, Feldman said. The call starts at 5 p.m. ET. "We believe revenue begins to show up in Q1 '27," Feldman said in the interview, adding that Microsoft signed the deal in October. Cerebras has also landed deals with other major cloud providers Amazon and Oracle . Cerebras is evaluating its financing options to meet the ramping demand, Feldman said in the interview. The company is trying to challenge Nvidia in the AI chip market. Its earnings land on the same day that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned from the company he co-founded after multiple scandals involving extramarital affairs. For the fourth quarter, Cerebras expects a core gross margin of 47% to 49%, with $310 million to $330 million in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for a 42.1% margin and $271 million in revenue. Cerebras said it expects revenue to triple in 2027. That implies about $2.85 billion in revenue. headlines.title: Cisco beats on earnings, says AI infrastructure revenue will double this fiscal year
headlines.summary: Cisco is trying to become a bigger player in AI after missing out on the early years of the boom.
headlines.article_text: Cisco (CSCO) Q1 2027 earnings Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Cisco reported fiscal first-quarter earnings that topped estimates. The computer networking company is trying to become a bigger player in AI after missing out on the early years of the boom. The stock is up 35% this year, trouncing the Nasdaq, which is up about 9%. In this article CSCO Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Cisco CEO Chuck Robbins appears at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, on Jan. 21, 2026. Krisztian Bocsi | Bloomberg | Getty Images Cisco shares rose in extended trading on Thursday after the maker of networking gear reported better-than-expected fiscal first-quarter results. Here's how the company did compared to LSEG consensus estimates: EPS: $1.40 adjusted vs. $1.33 expected Revenue: $18.5 billion vs. $18.1 billion expected. Revenue increased 24% from $14.88 billion a year earlier, Cisco said in a statement. Net income rose to $4.6 billion, or $1.14 per share, from $2.9 billion, or 72 center per share, a year ago. Cisco is trying to gain a foothold in the artificial intelligence buildout after missing out on the early years of the generative AI boom. The company's stock price is up about 35% this year as of Thursday's close, trouncing the Nasdaq, which has gained 9% over that stretch. Cisco raised its expectation for AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers to $9 billion this fiscal year, more than double the figure in fiscal 2026. "Organizations are turning to Cisco for our trusted, market-defining technology and our expertise to help them scale, secure and optimize their environments for the agentic AI era," CEO Chuck Robbins said in the statement . For the fiscal second quarter, Cisco said it expects revenue of between $18 billion and $18.2 billion, topping the average analyst estimate of $17.88 billion, according to LSEG. The company is projecting adjusted earnings per share of $1.34 to $1.36, beating the $1.23 average estimate.
